newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds continue rally on Brazil debt swap.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds continue rally on Brazil debt swap.

text.p: Argentine bonds were much higher late morning Wednesday as the already positive mood from steady U.S. rates was boosted further by news of a deal by Brazil to swap Brady debt.
"I think this market still has some room to go," said a trader at a local bank.
Prices started rallying Tuesday on news that the U.S. Federal Reserve held rates steady.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 was up 1/4 at 93-1/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 4 due 2002 was up $0.50 at 115.80.
But the biggest gainer in the morning was Argentina's Brady dicsount bond due 2023 which surge one point to 85-6/8.
Another trader said he had seen some genuine buyers entering the market when it initially surged Tuesday.
